fullPassage: When I was 12, I was passionate about soccer. Now, I prefer American football. I graduated in India with a computer science degree at 22, and now I’m a journalist and podcast host in the US. We change constantly, but we imagine ourselves staying the same. Our cells are always renewing, and our brains are always rewiring. So here is my advice. First, envision who you want to become and stay curious. Second, your future self may disagree with your current opinions, so be respectful of others. Third, your future self will have strengths you lack now, so don’t fear challenges.

questions.passage: Have you ever felt anxious about your own creativity? Do you blame yourself when brilliant ideas don’t come? ① The ancient Romans had a different view of creativity. ② The poet Ruth Stone described how, as a child working in the fields, she could feel a poem coming toward her like a thunderous train of air, shaking the earth under her feet. ③ When it reached her, she had to race to the house to grab a pencil and write it down. ④
questions.stem:
다음 글에서 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?

"They believed that a “genius” was not a gifted person but a kind of divine assistant spirit that lived in the walls of an artist’s studio."

det.korean: 고대 로마인들의 다른 관점을 소개한 직후, 그들이 genius를 어떻게 믿었는지 구체적으로 설명하는 문장이 와야 한다. 그 다음 Ruth Stone의 예시로 이어진다.
det.analysis:
✅ ②: "had a different view" 직후 → 그 관점의 구체적 설명 → 그리고 Stone의 예시
❌ ①: 아직 로마인 언급 전
❌ ③: Stone의 경험 도중 → 흐름 단절
❌ ④: Stone의 행동 완료 후 → 맥락 불일치
det.tip: 일반 소개 → 구체적 설명 → 예시: "had a different view" → "They believed..." → "Ruth Stone..."

questions.passage: We change constantly, but we imagine ourselves staying the same. ① Our cells are always renewing, and our brains are always rewiring. ② Think of the Ship of Theseus: if every piece of wood is replaced over time, is it still the same ship? ③ So here is my advice. ④
questions.stem:
다음 글에서 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?

"We are living examples of this paradox."

det.korean: 테세우스의 배 비유 직후, "우리는 이 역설의 살아 있는 예시이다"라는 연결 문장이 와야 한다. 그 다음 조언으로 이어진다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③: 테세우스의 배 역설 설명 직후 → "this paradox"의 지시대상 확보 → 조언으로 전환
❌ ①: 아직 역설 언급 전
❌ ②: 세포/뇌 설명과 배 비유 사이 → "this paradox" 지시 불명
❌ ④: 이미 조언 시작 후
det.tip: "this paradox" = 테세우스의 배 비유 → 반드시 그 직후에 와야 함

questions.passage: The writer’s own process was far less dramatic: just showing up at her desk every morning and working through boring routine. But ideas would come, mysteriously, when she was deeply engaged and immersed in the work. The message is clear: put __________________________________________, and your genius will come.
questions.stem:
다음 주어진 단어를 올바른 순서로 배열하시오.

heart / into / and / your / soul / work / your

det.korean: "your heart and soul into your work" → 일에 마음과 영혼을 쏟아라.
det.analysis:
put(동사) + your heart and soul(목적어) + into your work(전치사구)
put A into B = A를 B에 쏟다
det.tip: put + 목적어(your heart and soul) + into + 장소(your work)

questions.wa: your heart and soul into your work
accept: your heart and soul into your work
Your heart and soul into your work

questions.passage: So here is my advice. First, envision __________________________________________ and stay curious.
questions.stem:
다음 주어진 단어를 올바른 순서로 배열하시오.

become / you / to / want / who

det.korean: "who you want to become" → 되고 싶은 사람을 그려봐라.
det.analysis:
envision(동사) + who you want to become(간접의문문 목적어)
who(의문사) + you(주어) + want(동사) + to become(부정사)
det.tip: 간접의문문: 의문사 + 주어 + 동사 순서 (who you want, not who do you want)

questions.passage: The poet Ruth Stone ①<u>described</u> how, as a child ②<u>working</u> in the fields, she could feel a poem ③<u>coming</u> toward her like a thunderous train of air, ④<u>shaking</u> the earth under her feet. When it reached her, she had to race to the house to ⑤<u>grabbing</u> a pencil and write it down.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~⑤ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ⑤ grabbing → grab: to부정사 뒤에서 write과 병렬을 이루는 동사원형 grab이 적절하다. "to grab ... and write ..."
det.analysis:
❌ ⑤ grabbing: to + 동사원형 병렬 → to grab and write
✅ ① described: 과거형 → 올바름
✅ ② working: 현재분사 → a child를 수식
✅ ③ coming: 지각동사 feel + 목적어 + ~ing
✅ ④ shaking: 동시동작 분사구문
det.tip: to A and B: A와 B는 같은 형태(동사원형) → to grab and write

questions.passage: Think of the Ship of Theseus: if every piece of wood __________ over time, is it still the same ship?
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 목재가 교체되는 것이므로 수동태 is replaced가 적절하다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ is replaced: 수동태 → 목재가 교체되는 대상
❌ ① replace: 능동 원형 → 주어가 교체하는 것이 아님
❌ ② replaced: 과거형 → if절에서 현재 시제가 자연스러움
❌ ④ replacing: 현재분사 → if절 동사 자리에 부적절
det.tip: 주어가 동작을 당하는 경우 → 수동태(be + p.p.)

questions.passage: Have you ever felt ①<u>anxious</u> about your own creativity? Do you ②<u>blame</u> yourself when brilliant ideas don’t come? The ancient Romans had a different view of creativity. They believed that a "genius" was not a ③<u>humble</u> person but a kind of divine assistant spirit that lived in the walls of an artist’s ④<u>studio</u>. The message is clear: put your heart and ⑤<u>soul</u> into your work.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~⑤ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 원문은 "not a gifted person but a divine spirit"(재능 있는 사람이 아니라). ③ humble(겸손한)은 gifted의 반의어로 문맥에 부적절하다.
det.analysis:
❌ ③ humble(겸손한): 원문 gifted(재능 있는) → "not a gifted person but..."에서 대조되는 것
✅ ① anxious(불안한): 원문 일치
✅ ② blame(탓하다): 원문 일치
✅ ④ studio(작업실): 원문 일치
✅ ⑤ soul(영혼): 원문 일치
det.tip: gifted(재능 있는) ↔ humble(겸손한) — not A but B 구문에서 A에 해당하는 단어

questions.passage: The writer’s own process was far less dramatic: just showing up at her desk every morning and working through __________. But ideas would come, mysteriously, when she was deeply engaged and immersed in the work.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 필자의 과정은 극적이지 않았다: 매일 아침 책상에 앉아 지루한 일상(boring routine)을 거치는 것. 하지만 깊이 몰입하면 아이디어가 떠올랐다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ boring routine: "far less dramatic" + "just showing up" → 단조로운 일상
❌ ① physical training: 신체 훈련은 문맥과 무관
❌ ② artistic talent: 재능은 과정이 아님
❌ ③ formal education: 공식 교육은 문맥과 무관
det.tip: "far less dramatic" + "just showing up every morning" → 반복적이고 단조로운 과정

questions.passage: When I was 12, I was passionate about soccer. Now, I prefer American football. I graduated in India with a computer science degree at 22, and now I’m a journalist and podcast host in the US. We __________, but we imagine ourselves staying the same.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 축구에서 미식축구로, 인도에서 미국으로, 컴퓨터 공학에서 저널리즘으로 변화 → 우리는 끊임없이 변한다(change constantly).
det.analysis:
✅ ② changing constantly: 구체적 변화 예시 → 끊임없는 변화
❌ ① staying the same: "but we imagine ourselves staying the same"과 대조되어야 함
❌ ③ becoming weaker: 문맥에 없음
❌ ④ losing memories: 문맥에 없음
det.tip: but 대조: 빈칸(실제) ↔ "staying the same"(상상) → 실제로는 변한다

questions.passage: When I was 12, I was __________ (passion) about soccer. Now, I prefer American football.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 어법에 맞게 변형하여 쓰시오.

det.korean: passion(명사) → passionate(형용사): "was + 형용사" 구문. "축구에 열정적이었다"
det.analysis:
passion(명사) → passionate(형용사)
was + 형용사: 상태를 나타내는 2형식
be passionate about = ~에 열정적이다
det.tip: passion → passionate / compassion → compassionate — 명사 → -ate 형용사

questions.passage: Have you ever felt anxious about your own __________ (creative)? Do you blame yourself when brilliant ideas don’t come?
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 어법에 맞게 변형하여 쓰시오.

det.korean: creative(형용사) → creativity(명사): 소유격 your own 뒤에 명사가 필요. "당신 자신의 창의성"
det.analysis:
creative(형용사) → creativity(명사)
your own + 명사: 소유격 뒤에 명사 필요
your own creativity = 당신 자신의 창의성
det.tip: creative → creativity / active → activity — 형용사 → -ity 명사 변환

questions.passage: The poet Ruth Stone described how, as a child working in the fields, she could feel a poem coming toward her like a thunderous train of air, shaking the earth under her feet. When it reached her, she had to race to the house to grab a pencil and write it down.
questions.stem: 다음 글에서 Ruth Stone이 시가 다가왔을 때 집으로 달려가 잡아야 했던 것을 본문에서 1단어로 찾아 쓰시오.

det.korean: "she had to race to the house to grab a pencil and write it down" → 연필
det.analysis:
시가 다가왔을 때 집으로 달려가 잡은 것 = pencil
1단어 답 = pencil
det.tip: grab = 잡다 → 잡아야 했던 대상 = pencil(연필)

questions.passage: When I was 12, I was passionate about soccer. Now, I prefer American football. I graduated in India with a computer science degree at 22, and now I’m a journalist and podcast host in the US.
questions.stem: 다음 글에서 화자가 인도에서 22살에 받은 학위의 분야를 본문에서 2단어로 찾아 쓰시오.

det.korean: "I graduated in India with a computer science degree" → 컴퓨터 공학
det.analysis:
인도에서 받은 학위 분야 = computer science
2단어 답 = computer science
det.tip: graduated with a ___ degree: ~학위를 받고 졸업하다

questions.passage: Have you ever felt anxious about your own creativity? Do you blame yourself when brilliant ideas don’t come? The ancient Romans had a different view of creativity. They believed that a "genius" was not a gifted person but a kind of divine assistant spirit that lived in the walls of an artist’s studio. The poet Ruth Stone described how, as a child working in the fields, she could feel a poem coming toward her like a thunderous train of air, shaking the earth under her feet.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

det.korean: "feel a poem coming toward her like a thunderous train of air" → Stone은 시가 천둥 같은 공기의 기차처럼 다가오는 것을 느꼈다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② Stone이 시가 천둥치는 공기의 기차처럼 다가옴을 느낌: 일치
❌ ① genius는 "not a gifted person" → 재능 있는 사람이 아님
❌ ③ "far less dramatic" → 극적이지 않았음
❌ ④ "when deeply engaged and immersed" → 몰입할 때
det.tip: 비유 표현 "like a thunderous train of air"를 정확히 파악

ch: 고대 로마인들은 genius를 재능 있는 사람이라고 여겼다.
Ruth Stone은 시가 천둥치는 공기의 기차처럼 다가오는 것을 느꼈다.
아이디어는 불안할 때 가장 잘 떠올랐다.

questions.passage: When I was 12, I was passionate about soccer. Now, I prefer American football. I graduated in India with a computer science degree at 22, and now I’m a journalist and podcast host in the US. We change constantly, but we imagine ourselves staying the same. Our cells are always renewing, and our brains are always rewiring. So here is my advice. First, envision who you want to become and stay curious. Second, your future self may disagree with your current opinions, so be respectful of others. Third, your future self will have strengths you lack now, so don’t fear challenges.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

det.korean: 본문: "your future self may disagree with your current opinions, so be respectful" → 의견이 바뀔 수 있으니 존중하라는 뜻이지, "절대 바꾸지 말라"는 것이 아니다.
det.analysis:
❌ ④ 현재 의견을 절대 바꾸지 말라: 본문은 오히려 변할 수 있다고 인정하라는 조언
✅ ① "passionate about soccer" → 일치
✅ ② "graduated in India with a CS degree" → 일치
✅ ③ "cells are always renewing" → 일치
det.tip: "may disagree" = 동의하지 않을 수 있다 → 변화를 인정하라는 메시지

ch: 화자는 인도에서 컴퓨터 공학 학위를 받았다.
화자는 우리의 세포가 항상 새로워지고 있다고 했다.
화자는 현재 의견을 절대 바꾸지 말라고 조언했다.

questions.passage: The message is clear: put your heart and soul into your work, and your genius will come. First, envision who you want to become and stay curious. Second, your future self may disagree with your current opinions, so be respectful of others. Third, your future self will have strengths you lack now, so don’t fear challenges.
questions.stem: 이 글 전체의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 일에 전력하면 천재성이 온다 + 되고 싶은 자신을 그려라 + 도전을 두려워하지 말라 → 자기 개선과 변화를 받아들이는 삶
det.analysis:
✅ ③ 자기 개선과 변화: "put heart and soul" + "envision" + "don’t fear challenges"
❌ ① 축구/미식축구: 예시일 뿐
❌ ② 학문 비교: 주제 아님
❌ ④ 로마 예술: 보조 배경
det.tip: 두 강연의 공통 주제: 최선의 자신이 되기(Becoming the Best Possible Me)

questions.passage: The ancient Romans had a different view of creativity. They believed that a "genius" was not a gifted person but a kind of divine assistant spirit that lived in the walls of an artist’s studio.
questions.stem:
다음 진술이 본문의 내용과 일치하면 True, 일치하지 않으면 False를 고르시오.

"According to the ancient Romans, a genius was a divine spirit living in the walls of an artist’s studio."

det.korean: "a kind of divine assistant spirit that lived in the walls of an artist’s studio" → 본문과 일치 → True
det.analysis: ✅ True: "divine assistant spirit" + "lived in the walls" → 진술과 일치
det.tip: 진술의 핵심 요소(divine spirit + walls + studio)를 본문과 대조

questions.passage: The writer’s own process was far less dramatic: just showing up at her desk every morning and working through boring routine. But ideas would come, mysteriously, when she was deeply engaged and immersed in the work.
questions.stem:
다음 진술이 본문의 내용과 일치하면 True, 일치하지 않으면 False를 고르시오.

"The writer’s creative process was highly dramatic and exciting."

det.korean: 본문: "far less dramatic: just showing up ... boring routine" → 극적이지 않고 지루한 일상이었다. "highly dramatic"은 본문과 반대. → False
det.analysis: ❌ False: "far less dramatic" + "boring routine" ≠ "highly dramatic and exciting"
det.tip: far less dramatic = 훨씬 덜 극적인 → highly dramatic의 반대

questions.passage: We change constantly, but we imagine ourselves staying the same. Our cells are always renewing, and our brains are always rewiring. Think of the Ship of Theseus: if every piece of wood is replaced over time, is it still the same ship? We are living examples of this paradox.
questions.stem:
다음 진술이 본문의 내용과 일치하면 True, 일치하지 않으면 False를 고르시오.

"The speaker uses the Ship of Theseus as an analogy to explain that humans are constantly changing."

det.korean: 세포가 새로워지고 뇌가 재배선되는 것을 테세우스의 배에 비유하여 인간의 끊임없는 변화를 설명한다. → True
det.analysis: ✅ True: Ship of Theseus(비유) → cells renewing, brains rewiring(인간의 변화) → "We are living examples"
det.tip: analogy(비유) = 테세우스의 배를 통해 인간의 변화를 설명하는 것

questions.passage: So here is my advice. First, envision who you want to become and stay curious. Second, your future self may disagree with your current opinions, so be respectful of others. Third, your future self will have strengths you lack now, so don’t fear challenges.
questions.stem:
다음 진술이 본문의 내용과 일치하면 True, 일치하지 않으면 False를 고르시오.

"The speaker advises that we should fear challenges because our future self will be weaker."

det.korean: 본문: "your future self will have strengths you lack now, so don’t fear challenges" → 미래의 자신은 더 강해질 것이므로 두려워하지 말라. "약해질 것이므로 두려워하라"는 반대. → False
det.analysis: ❌ False: "will have strengths" ≠ "will be weaker", "don’t fear" ≠ "should fear"
det.tip: 두 가지 반대: strengths vs. weaker, don’t fear vs. should fear
